In detail

The Old Town — one of the largest surviving in Northern Europe, and where visitors stay. This is one of the few areas on this site rated green on a positive finding rather than on the absence of a negative one. Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT reported in 2026 that Vilnius is among Europe's safest capitals for tourists and that, unlike the big western capitals, it has no significant pickpocketing problem. The crimes that dominate Lithuanian figures are theft, domestic violence and — increasingly — fraud, none of which reshape an evening here. Registered crime in the Vilnius area fell in 2025 and clearance rose to 52%. Ordinary care, nothing more.

Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Frequently asked questions

Is Senamiestis safe?

Wandroz currently rates Senamiestis in Vilnius as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Vilnius, both by day and after dark. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Vilnius publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Senamiestis safe at night?

At night, Senamiestis is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Vilnius. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Senamiestis a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Senamiestis's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Vilnius) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
